scope: One-character source art only, four authored jump-chain keys in eight headings.

provenance.save_method: PowerShell Copy-Item; generated original copied byte-identically, no pixel modifications.

references.role: Primary current runtime costume, face, colors, body proportions and headings.
Supporting hooded treefolk identity, anatomy and rear/profile details.
Pixel-art style only; old labels, antlers, staff and effects explicitly excluded.

review.method: Original generated sheet visually inspected at source size; source and copy SHA256 compared; dimensions and alpha counted read-only.
observations: Exactly eight columns by four rows, all 32 full-body sprites complete, separated by transparent gutters without obvious cropping.
Green pointed gold-edged hood, dark wooden face with amber eyes, gold belt, layered leaf cape and bark limbs remain recognizable.
Requested front, front-right, right profile, back-right, full back, back-left, left profile and front-left sequence is present across the four rows.
Rise shows folded/tucked legs while descent opens and extends legs downward; landing is more compressed than anticipation.
Hands are empty; no staff, wand, baked spell, environment, captions, cell marks or ground shadow observed.
Skull/hood scale appears broadly stable across poses at source size; compression is articulated rather than visibly squash-scaled.
limitations: Broad leaf hood and cape partially obscure the underlying head boundary and rear knees; exact one-third neutral-standing head proportion requires lead comparison to the runtime atlas.
Rear-quarter leaf cape and overlapping limbs reduce fine leg readability; native-size silhouette legibility has not been tested.
Landing is visibly lower but not dramatically different from anticipation in some rear/profile headings; timing and native transition distinction remain unverified.
Generated alpha is largely partial rather than fully opaque. Deterministic threshold/hidden-RGB cleanup, registration, cropping and downsampling are lead-owned and NOT_RUN here.
No exact native skull continuity, body-volume or pixel-cluster comparison is claimed.
